items.decision_en: Keep the lift's degradation to codex's own documented default `on-request` with the operator notice; do not build a host replacement for `untrusted`'s routing on top of `granular`.

ledger_edits.why_en: Re-stamped at `rust-v0.150.1`: `approval_policy = "untrusted"` is fatal (the app-server exits 1 before answering `initialize`, upstream #39630) so the sandbox-off branch now degrades to `on-request` instead (`packages/codex-responses-adapter/src/config-writer.ts` symbol `UNBOUNDED_NEVER_DEGRADES_TO`), and because `SANDBOX_ENABLED_DEFAULT` is false (`packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts`) that branch is the SHIPPED DEFAULT — so on a default codex session an ordinary command raises no approval request and the three extracted floors get no subject, which the owner kept (answer QX4 = A, 2026-09-11, plan row P6.1062 `9375093b4`) with the residue made audible once per config write by `CODEX_UNBOUNDED_APPROVAL_NOTICE`.

Re-stamped at `rust-v0.150.1`: P2.197's repair rested on `untrusted`, the one public policy that stated a routing guarantee, and upstream retired it — the shipped binary refuses it fatally — so with the sandbox master switch off (the default, `SANDBOX_ENABLED_DEFAULT` false) every mode now emits `on-request` and no ordinary command reaches the host floor, while dangerous commands and sandbox-escalation requests still do; owner answer QX4 = A (2026-09-11, plan row P6.1062 `9375093b4`) keeps that posture with `CODEX_UNBOUNDED_APPROVAL_NOTICE` rather than reconstructing the routing host-side.

Read at the tag rather than from the names that remain: `granular` is NOT a successor to `untrusted` — in `core/src/exec_policy.rs` at `rust-v0.150.1` a non-dangerous command under an unrestricted filesystem sandbox answers `Allow` for `Never`, `OnRequest` AND `Granular(_)` (its own comment: "Mirror on-request behavior for unmatched commands"), only `UnlessTrusted` prompting — so teaching our validator the object variant buys a per-category vocabulary and no floor, and owner answer QX4 = A (2026-09-11, plan row P6.1062) refuses a host replacement built on it.

No behaviour changes. Re-stamps ledger rows A2, A7 and A64 (verdicts unchanged, Why cells updated).

items.flip_reason_en: One native survivor was read at the tag and should be seen once by the owner before it is forgotten: `core/src/config/mod.rs` still selects `UnlessTrusted` — the exact routing `untrusted` used to give us — when `active_project.is_untrusted()`, so the behaviour is reachable natively behind PROJECT TRUST, and the host wiring is S (mark the project untrusted on the sessions that used to ride the strict policy). It is not free: it asserts a trust state we do not mean and upstream also uses it to withhold project-level `AGENTS.md`, which is why the decision was taken the other way.

items.decision_en: Do not bundle `codex-code-mode-host`, `codex-path/rg` or `codex-resources/zsh` in 1.36.0; the follow-up plan decides by surface.

ledger_edits.why_en: This row's codex reason — "shells out to its own tooling, no bundled ripgrep" — is FALSE at `rust-v0.150.1`: the app-server release package is `codex-package.json` + `bin/codex-app-server` + `bin/codex-code-mode-host` + `codex-path/rg` + `codex-resources/zsh/bin/zsh`, and `scripts/fetch-codex.mjs` symbol `fetchTarget` installs only the app-server (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-codex-binary-provenance.md` §8.1), so codex DOES ship a ripgrep of its own that we deliberately leave out per owner answer QX5 = B (2026-09-11, plan row P6.1070); the verdict stays `n/a` because `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` is a claude env switch codex has no counterpart for.

A second, measured reason this cell cannot become `covered` by writing more `[features]` keys: three of the optional capabilities it names have no binary behind them in our install — `codex-resources/zsh/bin/zsh` (shell snapshot), `codex-path/rg` (file search) and `bin/codex-code-mode-host` (code mode) ship inside the same upstream package and are not fetched (`scripts/fetch-codex.mjs` symbol `fetchTarget`; provenance spec §8.1) — kept unbundled for 1.36.0 by owner answer QX5 = B (2026-09-11, plan row P6.1070), with boot proven unaffected.

items.flip_reason_en: The mechanism is native and already half-paid: the three binaries arrive inside the archive `scripts/fetch-codex.mjs` already downloads and verifies against the release `codex-package_SHA256SUMS`, so the wiring is S — extend `fetchTarget`'s extraction list and the dmg staging, adding pins per file exactly as the Windows trio has. What the refusal buys is dmg size for surfaces this fork does not expose; what it costs is that a `[features]` key an operator turns on for shell snapshots, file search or code mode has no binary behind it.
